description:
We are a team of curious, creative, and passionate individuals who believe in the power of science, technology, and collaboration to create meaningful innovations. Our interests include space exploration, planets and moons, Mars, satellites, artificial intelligence, coding, software development, graphic design, animation, and data visualization.

We aim to bring together different talents, ideas, and perspectives to develop creative solutions and explore exciting possibilities.
summary:
Ghost Machines is a game-based educational web app designed to keep users engaged through storytelling and interactive games while also providing NASA-based information on the machines and aircrafts deployed on the moon and Mars. It aims to target students, teachers, educational institutions, and space agencies. 

Every half a century, machines are sent out to perform missions on celestial bodies and slowly lose their place among NASA's active machines as their mission ends. School-aged space enthusiasts often hear only about active space machines, while the abandoned ones are left as artifacts of the surfaces or orbits of other planets. Ghost Machines' purpose is to bring to the user's remembrance the long-abandoned machines left on the moon and Mars in order to foster appreciation and inspiration among users through effective storytelling, dialogue, minigames, and user-centered features.
details:
Ghost Machines features an interactive storytelling through branching dialogue where users learn the stories and facts about the abandoned Machines. Some machines also feature mini games that are relevant to the machines' stories, making learning more engaging and sparking user curiosity to learn more about them. Additionally, the web app also includes direct quotes for each machine from the NASA resources which learners can choose to enable text-to-speech.
Through branching dialogue between the user and machines, the user establishes a personal connection with the machines. With the exact location of the machines, the web app highlights the machines' last known location, emphasizing that the machines are certainly not forgotten. In addition, the web app features a passport inspired system, after the user interacts with the machines and completes the minigames, they receive a stamp. The web app also features 3d models of the machines and their terrain.

BENEFITS:

Educational-storytelling

Learner engagement

Space agencies can avoid past failures by looking at the machines that pioneered and took part in the advancement of planet exploration.

IMPACTS:

Because young learners and above know only about the new and ongoing space missions, the web app gives the machines recognition, historical heritage, and honor for the machines' sacrifices.

HOW IT IS BUILT:

●      App: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, Vue Router, Pinia, vue-i18n, three.js, zod

●      Tests: Vitest (unit) and Playwright (browser)

●      Code checks: ESLint, oxlint, Prettier, vue-tsc

●      3D tools: gltf-transform, meshoptimizer

●      Fonts: Atkinson Hyperlegible, IBM Plex Sans Condensed, IBM Plex Mono, Fredoka, Silkscreen, Pixelify Sans

●      Server code: a small Laravel API (a health check)

●      Hosting: Vercel, at ghostmachines.app

HOW IS OUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

Ghost Machines features branching dialogue that makes users feel more emotionally connective to the machines.

Passport inspired system

3 looks (themes), plus a color-blind palette

2 languages: English and Filipino (458 lines each)

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED:

User engagement

User centered features

Emotionally appealing

Factualness
